prompt:
A card picture for a 1990s-style fantasy trading card game, hand-made traditional media with visible texture, the matte, slightly faded look of a printed 1990s card. One clear subject that fills the frame, its focal point near the centre, readable at a glance even very small. Keep the bottom-left and bottom-right corners dark and simple. Landscape 3:2. No text, no letters, no inscriptions, no border, no frame, no logo, no watermark, no signature. Not photorealistic, not 3D render, not modern digital concept art, not anime, not a glossy oil painting.

Setting: the War in Heaven, the final act of a dark card game: fallen angels, giants, demons, idolaters and the beasts of the Apocalypse (Genesis, 1 Enoch, Isaiah, Revelation and the old demonologies), painted the way medieval sacred art painted hell. The mood is frightening and intimidating: menace, dread and awe. Do not show Christ, God, saints or holy haloed figures. Where there is background, it may show distant battles between angels and demons, fire and ruin.

Look: a hand-coloured woodcut from an early printed Bible of the 1500s. Heavy black carved lines and dense parallel hatching cut into wood, coloured afterwards by hand with bright, transparent washes that slip outside the lines: sky blue, red lead, yellow, green and violet, on rough off-white rag paper with grain and foxing. Vigorous, slightly crude and dramatic, like the Apocalypse and Creation prints of the Reformation Bibles. Make it climactic and terrifying, a scene of awe and dread: towering scale, violent diagonal motion, deep black hatched shadows against blazing hellish light, the figure looming over the viewer.

Subject: The hero has fallen in the War in Heaven: a lone notched sword driven into a field of ash and a cracked shield lying at its foot, smoke drifting across the plain, under a vast blood-red sky in which tiny distant angels and demons still battle, the burning walls of a dark city far off on the horizon. Solemn and terrible.

Composition for a full-screen game-over screen, landscape 3:2: a wide, quiet scene with a low horizon. The upper-middle third is calm, dark, empty sky with no objects (a title will be printed there). The subject sits low and central, in the lower third, whole and uncropped, with breathing room on every side so it can be cropped to a wider or taller screen. The mood is solemn, mournful and still, not gory: a hero has fallen. No people's faces, no text.
